key_equations_and_data: §6.1 surface energy balance (area-normalised): C·dT_s/dt = α_sol·Q_sol + ε·Q_LW↓ − ε·σ·T_s⁴ − h·(T_s − T_air) − k·∂T/∂z|₀ + q_int, with C = ρ·c_p·δ [J·m⁻²·K⁻¹]. Implement absorbed solar as α_sol·Q_sol (prose line 363), NOT the (1−α_sol)^c form printed in the equation at line 355.

§6.1 / [R15] per-facet solar term (only hinted by the spec): Q_sol,facet = S·ψ·E_direct_normal + V_s·E_diffuse (+ optional ground-reflected albedo term), ψ = max(0, n̂·ŝ) illumination cosine, S ∈ {0,1} shadow flag. Requires a sun direction ŝ(t) from latitude, longitude and time — no solar-position algorithm is given anywhere in the spec.

§6.2 authored parameter set per material: h (derived, not authored), k [W·m⁻¹·K⁻¹], ε [–], α_sol [–], c_p [J·kg⁻¹·K⁻¹], ρ [kg·m⁻³]; plus δ from §12.3 `thickness_m`. Two-node needs δ1 and δ2 (§6.4) but §12.3 supplies one thickness.

§6.2 convection: h = max(h_free, a + b·v_wind^n), h_free = c·|T_s − T_air|^{1/3}; a = 5, b = 4, n = 0.8, c = 1.5 (SI, v in m/s). v_wind must be the relative air speed = wind + vehicle speed. Hand values: h(v=0, ΔT=0) = 5.00; h(v=28 m/s) = 62.52 W·m⁻²·K⁻¹; free branch wins at v=0 only for |ΔT| > (a/c)³ = 37.0 K.

§6.3 thermal inertia P = sqrt(k·ρ·c_p) [J·m⁻²·K⁻¹·s⁻½]; diurnal swing amplitude decreases and phase lag increases with P; crossover (contrast collapse) near sunrise/sunset is the acceptance phenomenon.

§6.4 two-node model: C1·dT1/dt = α_sol·Q_sol + ε·Q_LW↓ − ε·σ·T1⁴ − h·(T1 − T_air) − (T1 − T2)/R12 + q_int; C2·dT2/dt = (T1 − T2)/R12 − (T2 − T_deep)/R2d; R12 = δ1/(2k) + δ2/(2k). R2d and T_deep are used but never defined — must be defined (proposal: R2d = δ2/(2k) + δ_deep/k_deep, T_deep = running mean of T_air over the spin-up window).

§6.4 integrator and stability: explicit RK2, Δt in 1–60 s, stability Δt < 2·C1/(h + 4·ε·σ·T³ + 1/R12). Guard must be evaluated against the worst case over the weather series (max wind → max h, max plausible T) because h is time-varying. With §16.2 car-paint numbers (ρ=7800, c_p=470, k=45, δ=1.2 mm) C1 = 4399 J·m⁻²·K⁻¹ and 1/R12 = 37,500, giving Δt_max = 0.24 s — not the 60–200 s the spec claims (see inconsistencies).
§6.4 thermal tick: solver runs on a fixed tick (~1 Hz) decoupled from the render loop; render-time temperature is linearly interpolated between ticks.
§6.4 + skill: spin-up — initialise every node to T_air(t0 − H) with H = 24–48 h and integrate forward to t0; cache results keyed by (material hash, weather hash, start time).
§6.5 Newton cooling: dT/dt = −κ·(T − T∞); analytic T(t) = T∞ + (T0 − T∞)·e^{−κt}. Scope: scripted actors and no-solar relaxation only.

§6.6 active-source table (config defaults for PrescribedSolver schedules): engine bay +40…+90 K, τ 5–20 min; exhaust tip +80…+250 K, τ 2–10 min; tyres +10…+35 K, τ 10–30 min; brake discs +50…+400 K, 30 s heat / 5 min cool; catalytic converter +100…+300 K, 3–10 min; clothed human +8…+15 K (ε≈0.98); recently parked vehicle +5…+25 K decaying 20–60 min (Newton); road under departed vehicle −3…−8 K, 5–20 min.
Skill (heat traces): warm tyre trace +3…+10 K decaying over 5–20 min; cool body shadow −3…−8 K; implemented as additive decaying overlays on the ground temperature field.

Skill (vehicle regimes): five regimes — skin panels (LumpedTwoNode, environment driven), engine bay (Prescribed), driveline manifold→tips (Prescribed gradient), brakes & tyres (Prescribed from vehicle dynamics), glazing (LumpedTwoNode coupled to cabin) — plus a cabin-air node (greenhouse) that drives roof and glass from inside.

§5.3 sky temperature (needed for Q_LW↓): T_sky(θ_el) = T_air − ΔT_clear·(1 − cloud)·cos^q(θ_el); ΔT_clear ≈ 55–70 K (dry clear), 5–10 K (overcast/humid); q ≈ 0.5–1.0. The energy balance needs the hemispheric irradiance Q_LW↓ = ∫_hemisphere σ·T_sky(θ)⁴ cosθ dΩ blended with (1 − V_s)·σ·T_surround⁴ — this integral is not written in the spec and must be derived. Identity to test: cloud = 1 ⇒ Q_LW↓ = σ·T_air⁴ (= 390.1 W·m⁻² at 288 K).

§7.3 Magnus formula e_s(T) = 6.112·exp(17.67·T_C/(T_C + 243.5)) hPa, w = 216.7·RH·e_s/T_K — consumed by the atmosphere area from the SAME WeatherSeries (T_air, RH). Not implemented in thermal, but the WeatherSeries must carry RH for it.
§16.3 σ = 5.670 374 419 × 10⁻⁸ W·m⁻²·K⁻⁴ — already `irsim.radiometry.constants.SIGMA_SB`; thermal code imports it, never redefines it.

§12.3 material `thermal:` block fields: density_kg_m3, specific_heat_j_kgk, conductivity_w_mk, thickness_m, solar_absorptivity. No emissivity key here — ε comes from `optical.spectral_emissivity` (Kirchhoff non-negotiable).

Skill weather fields (no spec schema exists): time, air temperature [K], relative humidity [0–1], wind speed [m/s], cloud fraction [0–1], direct(-normal) and diffuse(-horizontal) solar irradiance [W·m⁻²], optional precipitation. Hourly is enough; interpolate. Data file location: data/weather/*.csv (format to be defined by ADR).

New scene/thermal config fields (absent from §12.2, required to run §6): latitude_deg, longitude_deg, utc_offset_h (or tz), start_datetime, weather_file, spin_up_hours (default 48), thermal_tick_s (default 1.0), vehicle speed source for h.
Non-negotiable #2 at the thermal boundary: integrate in float64, emit float32 minimum; encoded AOV boundary (§13.3) c = (T − 200)/800 is owned by the isaac area but consumes this field.

Downstream consumers of WeatherSeries (must be injectable, not file-reading): atmosphere §7 (T_air, RH, visibility), sky radiance §5.3 (T_air, cloud), optics self-emission §8.2 (T_housing coupled to ambient), detector §9.2 (T_FPA lumped model from ambient + power).

Tolerances from spec §15 Tier 1 and the skills: energy-balance equilibrium analytic vs numeric < 0.1 K; per-step energy conservation 1e-6 relative; spin-up 48 h vs 96 h < 0.5 K at t = 0; crossover within 1 h of dawn and dusk; float32 boundary < 10 mK.

work_items.title: WeatherSeries container with validation, interpolation and content hash
work_items.description: Create src/irsim/thermal/weather.py with an immutable `WeatherSeries` (float64 arrays: time_s monotonic, T_air_K, rh, wind_m_s, cloud_frac, solar_direct_normal_W_m2, solar_diffuse_W_m2, optional precip_mm_h) built from arrays only — it never opens a file. Provide `at(t)` linear interpolation returning a `WeatherSample`, `time_range`, and a SHA-256 `content_hash` used later as the spin-up cache key and as the atmosphere/thermal coupling check. Assert plausibility at construction (T_air within TEMPERATURE_MIN_K..MAX_K and > 150 K to catch Celsius, rh and cloud in [0,1], irradiance ≥ 0, time strictly increasing). Refuse extrapolation outside the series (raise). This object is the single source of weather for thermal AND atmosphere (non-negotiable 6).
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Interpolation identity: value at every sample node equals the stored value to 1e-12; value at the midpoint between two hourly samples equals the arithmetic mean of the neighbours to 1e-12 (catches off-by-one and wrong-axis interpolation).
Unit guard: T_air = 15.0 (Celsius passed as kelvin) raises ValueError; rh = 55 (percent instead of fraction) raises; negative irradiance raises; non-monotonic time raises.
No silent extrapolation: `at(t)` outside [t0, t1] raises rather than clamping.

Hash contract: two series differing by 0.01 K in a single T_air sample have different content_hash; the same arrays constructed twice give identical hashes (spin-up cache correctness depends on this).

work_items.title: Solar geometry and per-facet solar loading Q_sol = S·ψ·E_dir + V_s·E_dif
spec_refs: §6.1 ([R15] shadow flag S and illumination cosine ψ)
work_items.description: src/irsim/thermal/solar.py: (1) `sun_direction(lat_deg, lon_deg, datetime_utc)` returning elevation/azimuth and a unit vector via a standard low-cost algorithm (NOAA/Spencer-class, ±0.5° adequate for heat loading — ADR); (2) `solar_loading(normal, sun_dir, E_direct_normal, E_diffuse, sky_view, shadow)` returning Q_sol [W·m⁻²] per facet with ψ = max(0, n̂·ŝ), S ∈ {0,1}; optional ground-reflected term albedo·E_global·(1−V_s)/2. The absorbed term is α_sol·Q_sol, applied in the solver, not here. Engine-free: the shadow flag is an input (renderer or analytic supplies it).
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Solar-noon elevation on the equinox equals 90° − |latitude| to 0.5° at latitudes 0°, 45°N, 60°S; declination on 21 June within 0.1° of +23.44°; elevation at solar midnight at 45°N is negative all year (wrong sign conventions or a swapped lat/lon fail these).
Known-answer vs NOAA solar calculator at three recorded (date, lat, lon, UTC) points: elevation and azimuth within 0.5° (reference numbers recorded in the test with their source).

Facet cosine identities: horizontal facet ψ = sin(elevation) to 1e-12; south-facing vertical facet at solar noon in the northern hemisphere ψ = cos(elevation); north-facing vertical facet at that instant ψ = 0.

Shadow and energy: S = 0 removes exactly the direct term (residual equals V_s·E_dif); daily integral of Q_sol on a horizontal unshaded facet under the THM-02 synthetic day equals the analytic ∫E_dir·sin(el)dt + ∫E_dif dt to 0.1%.

work_items.title: Longwave downwelling irradiance Q_LW↓ from the §5.3 sky-temperature model
work_items.description: src/irsim/thermal/sky_longwave.py: `T_sky_elevation(T_air, cloud, theta_el, dT_clear=60, q=1)` (the single parametrisation shared with the radiance-path sky model — same function, one home) and `longwave_down(T_air, cloud, sky_view, T_surround, dT_clear, q)` = V_s·∫_hemi σ·T_sky(θ)⁴·cosθ dΩ/π-normalised + (1 − V_s)·σ·T_surround⁴, evaluated by fixed Gauss–Legendre quadrature in θ (closed form is not available for general q). Document that §5.3's T_sky is an LWIR brightness-temperature parametrisation being used as a broadband proxy (ADR).
depends_on: radiometry/atmosphere: §5.3 sky radiance model must import this same T_sky_elevation function (no second parametrisation)
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Overcast identity: cloud = 1 ⇒ Q_LW↓ = σ·T_air⁴ to 1e-9 relative (= 390.1 W·m⁻² at 288 K); any hemispheric-weighting bug breaks this.
Sky-view identity: V_s = 0 ⇒ Q_LW↓ = σ·T_surround⁴ to 1e-9; V_s = 1, cloud = 1, T_surround ≠ T_air ⇒ no dependence on T_surround.
Independent quadrature: Gauss–Legendre result vs brute-force 2-D trapezoid over (θ, φ) on a 2000×2000 grid agree to < 0.1 W·m⁻² (≈ 20 mK equivalent since dQ/dT = 4σT³ ≈ 5.4 W·m⁻²·K⁻¹ at 288 K).

Known-answer range: clear dry sky, T_air = 288 K, ΔT_clear = 60 K, q = 1, V_s = 1 gives Q_LW↓ in [230, 320] W·m⁻² (published clear-sky range) and at least 60 W·m⁻² below the overcast value; Q_LW↓ is monotonically increasing in cloud fraction.

work_items.title: TemperatureSolver protocol plus PrescribedSolver and NewtonCoolingSolver
work_items.description: src/irsim/thermal/solvers/base.py: `TemperatureSolver` Protocol — `advance(t, dt)`, `temperature() -> float64 array`, `state` (for caching), `dtype` guarantee. src/irsim/thermal/solvers/scripted.py: `PrescribedSolver` (time-series or callable of vehicle state, linear interpolation) and `NewtonCoolingSolver` (dT/dt = −κ(T − T∞), integrated with the exact exponential update so it is unconditionally stable; κ or τ = 1/κ from config). Docstring states the scope limit from §6.5: no solar, no cold-sky exchange.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Newton vs analytic: T(t) = T∞ + (T0 − T∞)·e^{−κt} at t = 3/κ agrees to < 1 mK for dt = τ/100, and the exact-update scheme also agrees to < 1 mK for dt = 5τ (no overshoot below T∞ — a naive explicit Euler would go negative here).
Time-varying T∞: with T∞(t) stepping at t1, the response after the step equals the analytic solution restarted from T(t1) to < 1 mK.
Prescribed: values at schedule nodes exact; between nodes equal to linear interpolation to 1e-12; a schedule with non-monotonic time raises.
Interface: every solver class in the package satisfies the Protocol under mypy strict (structural check), and `temperature()` never returns float16 (dtype assert).

work_items.title: Single-node surface energy balance: RHS, RK2 step, analytic steady state
work_items.description: src/irsim/thermal/energy_balance.py: `ThermalProperties` dataclass (density, specific_heat, conductivity, thickness, solar_absorptivity, emissivity — the last populated FROM the material's optical data by the materials loader, never authored in the thermal block), `SurfaceForcing` (Q_sol, Q_LW_down, T_air, v_rel, q_int), `net_flux(T, props, forcing)` implementing §6.1 without the conduction term, `rk2_step`, and `steady_state_temperature(props, forcing)` solving ε·Q_LW↓ + α·Q_sol + q_int − εσT⁴ − h(T)(T − T_air) = 0 by bracketing (scipy.optimize.brentq). Scalar reference implementation; float64.
depends_on: materials: (soft) ThermalProperties will be populated by the material loader; until then tests use §16.2 values in a fixture
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Analytic equilibrium: constant forcing, no solar, q_int = 0 — the solver run to t = 20·C/(h + 4εσT³) converges to the brentq root of the balance to < 0.1 K (§15 Tier 1); repeat with q_int = 50 W·m⁻² and with Q_sol = 600 W·m⁻² (root shifts; both < 0.1 K).
Energy conservation per step: C·(T_{n+1} − T_n) equals the RK2 quadrature of the net flux over the step to 1e-6 relative (skill test), for 1000 consecutive steps.
Linearised relaxation: a 1 K perturbation from equilibrium decays with e-folding time τ = C/(h + 4εσT_eq³); fitted τ within 1% of analytic (checks the T⁴ derivative and the sign of every term).
Monotone sensitivities: raising Q_sol raises T_eq; raising h moves T_eq toward T_air; ε = 0 removes both radiative terms exactly (T_eq → T_air + (αQ_sol + q_int)/h to 1e-9).

work_items.title: LumpedTwoNodeSolver (surface + substrate) with stability guard — scalar reference
work_items.description: src/irsim/thermal/solvers/two_node.py: the §6.4 system with R12 = δ1/(2k1) + δ2/(2k2) (allow distinct k per node, defaulting to one k), an explicitly defined R2d and T_deep (ADR: R2d = δ2/(2k2) + δ_deep/k2; T_deep = running mean of T_air over the spin-up window or a config value), RK2 integration, and a constructor guard raising ValueError when Δt ≥ 2·C1/(h_max + 4εσT_max³ + 1/R12) using the worst-case h over the injected WeatherSeries (max wind + vehicle speed) and T_max = 400 K; also a per-step assert. Emit total stored energy for conservation tests.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Reduction: R12 → ∞ (substrate decoupled) reproduces the THM-07 single-node trajectory to < 0.1 mK over 24 h; C2 → ∞ with T2 = T_deep reproduces a single node with an added conductive sink whose analytic equilibrium is checked by brentq to < 0.1 K.
Two-node analytic equilibrium: constant forcing — eliminate T2 = (T1/R12 + T_deep/R2d)/(1/R12 + 1/R2d), brentq the scalar residual, run solver to steady state: both nodes within 0.1 K of the roots.
Linear-limit oracle: with the radiation term linearised about T_eq (ΔT ≤ 2 K) the 2×2 linear system solved by scipy.linalg.expm matches the RK2 trajectory to < 10 mK over 6 h at Δt = 10 s.

Stability guard: dt = 1.1 × bound raises ValueError at construction; dt = 0.9 × bound does not; with §16.2 car-paint numbers and a 1.2 mm substrate the computed bound is 0.235 ± 0.005 s (documents the spec's inconsistency numerically).
Energy conservation: C1·ΔT1 + C2·ΔT2 over the run equals the integrated boundary fluxes (solar + LW − emission − convection − deep conduction) to 1e-6 relative.

Thermal inertia ordering (§6.3): under identical sinusoidal forcing, the T1 swing amplitude strictly decreases and the phase lag strictly increases across dry soil (P≈600), asphalt (P≈1230), concrete (P≈1680), water (P≈1580 with δ) — assert ordering by P.

work_items.title: Spin-up with cache keyed by (material hash, weather hash, start time)
work_items.description: src/irsim/thermal/spinup.py: `spin_up(solver_factory, weather, t0, hours=48)` initialises all nodes to T_air(t0 − hours) and integrates to t0 using the same tick; an in-memory (optionally on-disk under an ignored cache dir — ADR) cache keyed by (ThermalProperties hash, WeatherSeries.content_hash, t0, hours, dt). Per material class × orientation bin, not per facet, at L2 (ADR).
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Convergence: 48 h vs 96 h spin-up agree at t0 to < 0.5 K for dry asphalt and thin painted steel under the checked-in weather file (skill); for 0.3 m concrete the difference is reported and asserted < 1.0 K (documented looser bound — high inertia).
Initial condition: at t0 − hours every node equals T_air(t0 − hours) exactly; with a constant-weather series the spun-up state equals the THM-08 analytic equilibrium to < 0.1 K.

Cache semantics: a second call with identical keys returns bit-identical state and performs zero integration steps (step counter spy); perturbing one weather sample by 0.01 K or changing t0 by 1 s invalidates the cache.

work_items.title: ThermalField tick scheduler with render-time interpolation and float32 output boundary
spec_refs: §1 'separate the temperature problem from the radiance problem'
work_items.description: src/irsim/thermal/field.py: `ThermalField` owns the facet solver, advances on a fixed tick (default 1.0 s) driven by scene time, and answers `temperature_at(t_render) -> float32 array` by linear interpolation between the last two ticks; queries never mutate state. Asserts output dtype is float32 or float64 (never float16). This is the object the isaac glue reads each frame.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Interpolation identity: at t between ticks t_k and t_{k+1}, output equals (1−w)·T_k + w·T_{k+1} to 1e-12 (computed independently from the recorded tick values); at tick instants exact.
Precision boundary: float64 internal trajectory vs the float32 output over a 48 h run differs by < 10 mK everywhere (ir-sim-testing encode/decode tolerance); requesting float16 raises.

Decoupling and determinism: 3600 render queries at 60 Hz between two ticks leave the solver state hash unchanged; two runs with identical inputs are bit-identical (there is no randomness in the thermal path — noise belongs in radiance space, non-negotiable 3).

work_items.title: Tier-3 diurnal phenomenology tests and validation script (crossover, inertia, overcast, wind, vehicle speed)
work_items.description: tests/unit/test_thermal_diurnal.py (marked slow if > 1 s, but must stay inside the 30 s unit budget — use Δt = 60 s) plus scripts/validate_thermal_diurnal.py producing a 24 h plot for the manual pass. Uses the checked-in clear-day weather at 45°N with solar noon at 12:00 local, §16.2 materials, and the full THM-04/05/08/10 chain.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Diurnal shape (dry asphalt): T_max occurs within [13:00, 16:00] local and T_min within ±90 min of sunrise; peak-to-peak swing in [15, 40] K on a clear summer day (a solver that is not running gives ~0 swing; a missing inertia term peaks at noon).
Thermal crossover: sign of (T_asphalt − T_thin_painted_steel) changes within ±60 min of sunrise and again within ±60 min of sunset (skill tolerance 1 h).
Overcast flattens: cloud = 1 reduces the asphalt swing by > 30% and the night-time |T_asphalt − T_metal| by > 30% relative to clear sky (§5.3 'flat on cloudy days').

Wind: doubling wind speed from 2 to 4 m/s lowers the asphalt T_max by > 1 K; vehicle-speed effect: a black painted hood panel at 28 m/s vs 0 m/s under 800 W·m⁻² differs by > 3 K at 14:00 (skill 'meaningful margin', quantified).
Wet vs dry soil (§16.2 rows): wet soil daytime T_max is lower than dry soil by > 2 K and its swing is smaller (Tier 3 'wet reads colder than dry').

work_items.title: Cabin-air node coupled to panels and glazing (vehicle greenhouse)
work_items.description: src/irsim/thermal/vehicle/cabin.py: one lumped cabin-air node C_cab with solar gain through glazing (τ_glass_solar from the material), convective exchange with the interior faces of roof, doors, glass (h_int ≈ 3–5 W·m⁻²·K⁻¹, config), and infiltration/HVAC term to ambient; panels become single-node (thin metal, no substrate — see ADR on stiffness) with the cabin node as their back-side boundary instead of T_deep. Glazing solved as LumpedTwoNode coupled to cabin.
depends_on: materials: glass solar transmittance per band (soft; test uses a constant)
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Greenhouse effect: at 14:00 under the clear day, roof T with the cabin node enabled exceeds roof T with the back side held at T_air by > 2 K (skill: without it 'daytime roofs come out too cold').
Coupled analytic equilibrium: constant forcing — cabin and each panel converge to the roots of the coupled algebraic system (solved independently with scipy.optimize.fsolve) to < 0.1 K.
Energy conservation of the coupled system (panels + glass + cabin): stored energy change equals integrated boundary fluxes to 1e-6 relative.
Night relaxation: with no solar, cabin excess over ambient decays with the analytic time constant of the coupled linearised system to 2%.

work_items.title: Prescribed vehicle heat-source schedules: engine bay, driveline gradient, brakes, tyres
work_items.description: src/irsim/thermal/vehicle/sources.py: `EngineBaySchedule` (ΔT(t) = ΔT_max·(1 − e^{−t/τ}) on ignition, Newton decay on shutdown), `DrivelineGradient` (monotone ΔT along manifold→cat→pipe→tip, each an exponential warm-up with its own τ), `BrakeDisc` (heat input from braking power P = m·v·a·share / n_discs into m_disc·c_p, Newton cooling with τ_cool), `TyreSchedule` (ΔT = ΔT_max·(1 − e^{−t/τ}) scaled by speed and lateral load). All are PrescribedSolver implementations driven by a `VehicleState(t, speed, accel, ignition, braking)` trace. Defaults from the §6.6 table, marked ESTIMATED.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Engine warm-up: ΔT at t = τ equals (1 − e⁻¹)·ΔT_max to 1 mK; steady ΔT within +40…+90 K for defaults; on shutdown the decay matches the Newton analytic to 1 mK.

Brake energy balance: for a 1500 kg vehicle braking 28 → 0 m/s with 70% front share on two discs of 8 kg steel, ΔT_disc = E/(m·c_p) analytically (independent arithmetic in the test) to 1e-6 relative, then Newton cool-down analytic to 1 mK; peak within +50…+400 K.
Tyre: ΔT strictly increasing with speed, saturating within +10…+35 K for defaults; zero speed for > 3τ returns to ambient within 1 mK.
Driveline: T_manifold > T_cat > T_pipe > T_tip at all times after warm-up; tip ΔT within +80…+250 K; catalytic converter within +100…+300 K.
Determinism: identical VehicleState traces give bit-identical schedules.

work_items.title: Environmental heat-trace overlays on the ground temperature field (tyre traces, body shadows)
spec_refs: §6.6 last row 'Road under a departed vehicle'
§15 Tier 3 'departed vehicle leaves a warm tyre trace and a cool body shadow'
work_items.description: src/irsim/thermal/traces.py: `HeatTraceLayer` holding a list of (footprint mask on a 2-D ground grid, amplitude ΔT0, τ, t_start) events; `apply(T_ground, t)` adds Σ ΔT0·e^{−(t − t_start)/τ} on each footprint. `tyre_trace_from_trajectory(points, track_width, tyre_width, grid)` and `body_shadow_from_pose(rect, grid)` rasterise footprints. Defaults: tyre +5 K τ 10 min, shadow −5 K τ 10 min (skill ranges). Engine-free on NumPy arrays; the isaac glue only supplies trajectories.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Exponential decay: overlay amplitude at t = t_start + τ equals ΔT0/e to 1 mK; at t = t_start + 5τ below 1% of ΔT0.
Superposition and locality: two overlapping traces add linearly to 1e-12; cells outside every footprint are bit-identical to the input field.

Rasterisation known answer: a straight trajectory along x with track width 1.5 m and tyre width 0.2 m on a 0.1 m grid marks exactly the two expected stripes (mask equality with an independently constructed mask).
Sign and range: tyre traces are positive and within +3…+10 K, body shadows negative and within −3…−8 K for defaults.

work_items.title: SlabSolver (1-D N-node diffusion, THERM-class) — L3 upgrade path and two-node error bound
work_items.description: src/irsim/thermal/solvers/slab.py: N-node 1-D conduction with the §6.1 surface boundary condition at node 0 and a fixed-T or zero-flux bottom boundary, implicit (backward Euler or Crank–Nicolson) conduction so Δt is not stiffness-limited, explicit surface fluxes. Same TemperatureSolver interface. Its main purpose at this stage is to quantify the two-node approximation error for the ADR; it is optional for L2.
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Semi-infinite periodic known answer: with surface T forced sinusoidally at period 24 h, amplitude at depth z decays as e^{−z/d} and lags by z/d, d = sqrt(2α/ω), α = k/(ρc_p): amplitude ratio within 2%, phase within 5° at z = d and z = 2d.
Steady conduction: fixed end temperatures give a linear profile to 1e-9 K; energy conservation to 1e-6 relative.

Two-node error bound: for dry asphalt over the checked-in 48 h weather, slab vs two-node surface temperature RMS difference < 1.5 K and max < 3 K (the number goes into the ADR; failure means the two-node δ1/δ2 defaults are wrong).
Stiffness: a 1 mm steel slab at Δt = 60 s integrates without divergence (implicit conduction), unlike the explicit two-node bound of 0.24 s.

work_items.title: ImportedSolver: precomputed per-facet temperature series from an external tool
work_items.description: src/irsim/thermal/solvers/imported.py: loads a .npz (time_s, facet_ids, T_K float32/float64) and serves linearly interpolated temperatures through the TemperatureSolver interface; refuses float16 or non-Kelvin data (plausibility guard).
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Round trip: a series written from a THM-09 run and re-imported reproduces the solver output bit-exact at sample times and to 1e-12 of linear interpolation between them.
Guards: a float16 array raises; values of 20.0 (Celsius) raise; facet id mismatch with the scene raises loudly rather than defaulting.

work_items.title: Thermal configuration schema: material thermal block, scene/site/time, weather binding — and the single-weather-object contract
work_items.description: src/irsim/config/thermal.py (pydantic v2): `MaterialThermalConfig` (density_kg_m3 > 0, specific_heat_j_kgk > 0, conductivity_w_mk > 0, thickness_m > 0, optional substrate_thickness_m, solar_absorptivity ∈ [0,1]; `extra='forbid'` so an `emissivity` key inside `thermal:` is rejected — ε is derived from optical data), `ThermalSceneConfig` (latitude_deg, longitude_deg, utc_offset_h, start_datetime, weather_file, spin_up_hours=48, thermal_tick_s=1.0, deep_temperature_mode). A `Scene` builder loads the weather ONCE and injects the same WeatherSeries instance into ThermalField and the atmosphere object; neither accepts a path.
depends_on: config: pydantic schema base / loader conventions
atmosphere: Atmosphere constructor must take a WeatherSeries (contract, not code dependency)
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Schema physics guards: negative thickness, α_sol = 1.2, missing conductivity, and an `emissivity` key under `thermal:` all raise ValidationError; the §12.3 example block validates and round-trips into ThermalProperties with the correct SI values (density 7800, thickness 0.0012).

Non-negotiable 6 by construction: ThermalField(...) and Atmosphere(...) constructors have no `weather_file` parameter (introspection test) and require a WeatherSeries; building a Scene yields `thermal.weather is atmosphere.weather` (identity) and equal content_hash; a Scene helper given two different weather objects raises.
Time handling: a start_datetime without timezone info is rejected; the resolved UTC start maps to the correct row of the weather file (known-answer).

work_items.title: Isaac Sim thermal tick driver: push ThermalField temperatures to per-prim encoded emission and read per-prim sky-view/shadow
work_items.description: src/irsim_isaac/thermal_driver.py: maps scene prims → facet indices (material class × orientation bin × shadow state), reads baked per-prim sky-view factor and a per-tick solar shadow flag (from a shadow probe or analytic), advances ThermalField on the physics tick, and writes the encoded temperature c = (T − 200)/800 into the float32 emission channel each render frame. Integration tests under tests/integration marked @pytest.mark.isaac.
depends_on: isaac: temperature encode/decode round trip < 10 mK (§16.4 step 2) must pass first
isaac: per-prim material mapping layer (materials area) providing material class per prim
tests_that_would_fail_if_physics_wrong: Round trip through the renderer: assign solver temperatures to 100 prims spanning 250–450 K, render, decode the AOV, compare to ThermalField output: max error < 10 mK (a float16 emission path fails at 0.25 K).

Tier-3 crossover on a demo scene (asphalt, concrete, painted vehicle, grass): automated contrast metric — standard deviation of decoded apparent temperature across material classes at 06:00 and 19:00 local is < 40% of its 13:00 value (spec §6.3 'does the scene go flat at 0600 and 1900').
Tick/frame consistency: temperatures decoded from two consecutive frames within one thermal tick differ by exactly the interpolation increment predicted by THM-11 (to 10 mK).
Performance guard: a 1 Hz update of 10,000 prims completes in < 100 ms (measured; if it fails, the per-prim attribute strategy must change — see risks).

decisions_needing_adr.title: Time integrator and stiffness handling for the two-node model (explicit RK2 vs semi-implicit conduction / exponential integrator)
decisions_needing_adr.why: The spec prescribes explicit RK2 at 1–60 s, but with §16.2 thin-metal numbers and a substrate node the stability bound is 0.24 s (1/R12 = 37,500 W·m⁻²·K⁻¹). Either thin panels are modelled as single nodes with a resistive back boundary (cabin/air), or conduction coupling is treated implicitly. This choice fixes the tick rate, the cost of spin-up, and which materials are representable.
options: Explicit RK2 as specified, with a constructor guard, and panels as single nodes coupled resistively to the cabin node (R = 1/h_int) rather than through δ/(2k)
Semi-implicit scheme: implicit (linear) conduction coupling and linearised radiation, explicit solar/convection — unconditionally stable at 1–60 s for every material
Exponential (Rosenbrock/ETD) integrator on the linearised system — exact for the stiff linear part, more code

decisions_needing_adr.title: Two-node lumped model as the L2 fidelity level, with defined R2d, T_deep, δ1/δ2 and a quantified error bound
decisions_needing_adr.why: The spec leaves R2d and T_deep undefined and gives one `thickness_m` per material while the model needs two. The two-node vs 1-D slab error (target < 1.5 K RMS for asphalt) must be measured and recorded so a reviewer can tell a deliberate approximation from a bug.
options: Two-node with δ1 = authored thickness, δ2 = per-material default (e.g. 0.2 m ground, none for panels), R2d = δ2/(2k) + δ_deep/k, T_deep = spin-up-window mean of T_air
Two-node with T_deep authored per scene (config) and R2d authored per material
Skip two-node and go straight to the implicit slab solver for ground materials (L3 for the ground only)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Convection parameterisation: spec §6.2 max(free, a + b·v^n) with a=5, b=4, n=0.8, c=1.5, relative speed as |wind| + |vehicle speed|
decisions_needing_adr.why: h is the largest uncertainty in the whole temperature prediction (§6.2). The chosen form makes the free-convection branch irrelevant below |ΔT| = 37 K at rest, and scalar speed composition ignores heading. Alternatives (Jürges/McAdams 5.7 + 3.8v, Palyvos, surface-orientation-dependent correlations) give 20–40% different h; the consequence is a multi-kelvin bias that Tier 4 will attribute elsewhere.
options: Spec form exactly (a, b, n, c as constants in a params dataclass)
Spec form with vector wind composition (wind vector minus vehicle velocity, per-facet orientation factor)
Surface-class-specific correlations (horizontal up/down, vertical) from ASHRAE/Palyvos

decisions_needing_adr.title: Weather data file format and interpolation contract
decisions_needing_adr.why: data/weather is empty and no format is specified. The format decides unit conventions (K vs °C, RH fraction vs percent, direct-normal vs global-horizontal irradiance), time-zone handling, and whether EPW/TMY files can be used directly. Interpolation (linear hourly) determines the temporal smoothness of the forcing.
options: Project CSV: ISO-8601 UTC timestamps, SI columns, direct-normal + diffuse-horizontal, hourly, linear interpolation
EPW (EnergyPlus weather) files with a converter — richer, widely available, but °C, Wh/m², local-time rows and no cloud fraction as such
Both: EPW → project CSV conversion script, and only the project CSV is loaded at runtime

decisions_needing_adr.title: Solar geometry source and shadow-flag source
decisions_needing_adr.why: The energy balance needs sun direction per facet and a shadow flag; the spec never says how to obtain either. Computing sun position requires site latitude/longitude/time in the scene config (not in §12.2); shadows over the 48 h spin-up cannot come from the renderer.
options: Compute sun position in irsim (NOAA/Spencer algorithm, ±0.5°) and take the shadow flag as an input: analytic (unshadowed) during spin-up, renderer-derived at run time
Read sun elevation/azimuth columns from the weather file (no algorithm, but every file must carry them)
Depend on an external library (pvlib/astropy) — accurate but adds a dependency to the engine-free core

decisions_needing_adr.title: Longwave sky model: one T_sky(θ_el) parametrisation (§5.3) shared by the radiance path and the energy balance, integrated hemispherically; LWIR-band ε used as the broadband ε
decisions_needing_adr.why: §5.3's T_sky is explicitly an LWIR brightness temperature, while §6.1 needs broadband Q_LW↓ [W·m⁻²]; standard alternatives (Brunt, Swinbank, Idso–Jackson sky emissivity from T_air and vapour pressure) are broadband but would introduce a second sky model that can drift from the one the camera sees. Which ε enters the balance (LWIR band vs total hemispherical) is also undefined.
options: Single §5.3 parametrisation, hemispherically integrated by Gauss–Legendre, ε_LWIR as broadband proxy (consistent but approximate)
Broadband sky-emissivity correlation (Brunt/Idso) for Q_LW↓ and §5.3 for the radiance path, with a consistency test between them
Spectral sky model integrated per band and broadband — correct, expensive, needs data not in the repo

decisions_needing_adr.title: Numerical precision policy for the thermal path: float64 internally, float32 at the field boundary
decisions_needing_adr.why: Non-negotiable 2 requires float32 or better; 48 h at 1 s ticks is 172,800 steps and float32 accumulation of ~1e-3 K increments can lose 10 mK-class precision. The decision also fixes the dtype the isaac encoding consumes.
options: float64 internal state, float32 output with assert (recommended)
float32 throughout with Kahan/compensated accumulation
float64 throughout including the encoded AOV (if the renderer supports it)

decisions_needing_adr.title: Thermal tick rate, interpolation, and solve granularity (per material class × orientation bin vs per facet)
decisions_needing_adr.why: Per-facet solving of a whole scene through a 48 h spin-up is expensive; per-material-class solving ignores orientation-dependent solar loading (south wall vs north wall) and per-facet shadowing. The choice bounds both the compute cost and the spatial realism of the temperature field.
options: Class × orientation-bin × shadow-state solve at 1 Hz, linear interpolation (L2)
Per-facet solve at 1 Hz for objects, class-level for terrain
Per-facet everywhere, GPU-side (Warp) — engine-bound, contradicts engine-free core unless mirrored in NumPy

decisions_needing_adr.title: Spin-up default length (48 h) and cache location/policy
decisions_needing_adr.why: Spin-up is mandatory (§6.4) and its result is keyed on weather content; caching to disk changes reproducibility and repository hygiene (which paths are ignored), and the default length trades correctness for high-inertia materials (concrete, water) against cost.
options: 48 h default, in-memory LRU cache only
48 h default, on-disk cache under an ignored directory keyed by hash, invalidated by content_hash
Adaptive: extend spin-up until the 24 h-apart state difference < 0.5 K

decisions_needing_adr.title: Vehicle thermal architecture: prescribed (measured) schedules for engine bay, driveline, brakes, tyres; solved panels and glazing; one cabin-air node
decisions_needing_adr.why: This is the 'measure, don't model' decision from the skill and §6.6. It puts the largest scene signal on data (thermocouple warm-up curves) rather than physics, defines what a vehicle asset must be annotated with, and sets the L2 boundary that Appendix A item 1 (no 3-D conduction) describes.
options: Prescribed schedules with §6.6 defaults marked ESTIMATED, replaced by measured curves later
Lumped multi-node engine/exhaust model with internal generation (more physics, largest uncertainty)
Import per-facet temperatures from MuSES/DIRSIG-class tools (ImportedSolver) for vehicles only

decisions_needing_adr.title: Environmental heat traces as decaying additive overlays rather than solved ground conduction
decisions_needing_adr.why: Overlays are cheap and match the phenomenology (§15 Tier 3), but they are not energy-conserving and their amplitudes/time constants are authored, not predicted. A reviewer must know this is deliberate.
options: Additive exponential overlays with authored ranges (skill values)
Local perturbation of the ground solver's surface node (energy-consistent, needs footprint history in the solver state)
No traces at L2 (documented gap)

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §6.1 prints absorbed solar as (1−α_sol)^c·Q_sol (line 355) while the prose (line 363), §6.4 (line 406) and the skill use α_sol·Q_sol. The printed form also has a stray superscript c.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Implement α_sol·Q_sol; add the monotone test in THM-07 (raising α_sol raises T_eq) — the complement form would make it fall. Note the resolution in the THM-07 docstring.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: §6.4's stability worked example ('thin painted metal, C1 ~ 5 kJ·m⁻²·K⁻¹ … 60–200 s') is only true if the 1/R12 term is dropped. With §16.2 car paint (k = 45, δ = 1.2 mm) 1/R12 = 37,500 and Δt_max = 0.235 s; the '60–200 s' figure corresponds to a lone node (837 s) with no substrate coupling.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: The THM-08 stability test computes the bound from §16.2 numbers and asserts 0.235 ± 0.005 s. Resolve via the integrator ADR (panels as single nodes with resistive back boundary, or implicit conduction).

ambiguities_and_risks.description: R2d and T_deep appear in §6.4 but are never defined; §12.3 supplies a single `thickness_m` whereas the two-node model needs δ1 and δ2.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Define both in the two-node ADR; THM-16 (slab) quantifies the error of the chosen δ2/R2d/T_deep defaults for asphalt (< 1.5 K RMS) — if that fails, the defaults are wrong.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Q_LW↓ is not given as a formula. §5.3's T_sky(θ_el) is an LWIR brightness-temperature model ('reads above +10 °C in MWIR'), not broadband; using it in the §6.1 energy balance is a proxy. The value of ΔT_clear also depends on humidity, which the spec mentions qualitatively only.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: THM-05 known-answer range test (230–320 W·m⁻² clear at 288 K, 390 W·m⁻² overcast) against published clear-sky longwave values; compare the proxy against a Brunt/Idso correlation across T_air 260–310 K and record the discrepancy in the sky-model ADR.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: No solar-position algorithm, site coordinates, or time-zone handling exists anywhere in the spec; Q_sol per facet (direct/diffuse split, illumination cosine, shadow flag) is only hinted via [R15]. The skill's weather fields include direct and diffuse irradiance but not how they combine with facet orientation.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: THM-04 known-answer tests against NOAA solar calculator values (record three reference points with source) and the equinox/solstice identities; ADR on solar geometry source.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Weather file format, units and interpolation are undefined; data/weather is empty. EPW files are in °C, Wh/m², local time, and lack a cloud fraction column, so a naïve loader will silently mis-scale.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: THM-02 loader tests with explicit unit headers (a '°C' file must load 273.15 higher than a 'K' file with the same numbers); define the format in an ADR before any weather-dependent test is written.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The skill says to assert the stability limit 'at solver construction', but h depends on wind (time-varying) and vehicle speed, and the T³ term on the current temperature — a construction-time check needs a worst-case bound the spec does not specify.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: THM-08 evaluates the bound with max wind + max vehicle speed over the injected WeatherSeries and T_max = 400 K at construction, and re-asserts per step; a test constructs with a weather series whose max wind pushes dt over the bound and expects ValueError.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Which emissivity enters the energy balance is undefined: §6.2 calls ε 'spectral', but the balance needs a single hemispherical broadband ε; the material library authors ε(λ) or ρ(λ) (Kirchhoff). Using LWIR-band ε for both absorption of Q_LW↓ and emission is an approximation (true for grey bodies only).
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Populate ThermalProperties.emissivity from the material's authored optical data in the loader (never a separate thermal-block key — THM-18 rejects one); compare LWIR-band ε vs a 3–50 µm weighted ε for a spectrally structured material (glass) once spectra exist and record the difference.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Spin-up convergence tolerance (48 h vs 96 h < 0.5 K) may not hold for high-inertia materials (0.3 m concrete, deep water) whose substrate time constant exceeds 48 h.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: THM-10 reports the 48-vs-96 h difference per material; if concrete exceeds 0.5 K, either lengthen the default or make spin-up adaptive (ADR), rather than loosening the tolerance.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The Tier-3 diurnal test criteria ('max near 1400–1500 local', 'crossover within an hour of dawn/dusk', 'meaningful margin' for vehicle speed) are qualitative and depend on the chosen solar-noon/time-zone convention and on §16.2 literature values that the spec itself says to replace.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: THM-12 fixes the site so solar noon = 12:00 local, widens the window to 13:00–16:00 with a comment, and quantifies 'meaningful' as > 3 K; the validation script produces the plot for a manual pass so a failure can be inspected rather than guessed at.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The convection form makes free convection essentially inactive (needs |ΔT| > 37 K at rest), so a still-air night surface cools only through radiation and a=5 forced floor — plausible but unvalidated; h is the largest single uncertainty (§6.2).
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Sensitivity report in scripts/validate_thermal_diurnal.py: asphalt T_min under a = 3, 5, 7 — if night-time T_min moves by > 2 K, flag for Tier-4 calibration and record in the convection ADR.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Isaac Sim 6.0: how the per-prim temperature reaches the renderer each tick is uncertain — per-prim OmniPBR emissive-colour writes (§13.1) are USD attribute updates whose float32 precision and per-frame cost for thousands of prims are undocumented; PtSelfIllumination availability/format as float32 is asserted by the spec but not verified.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: The isaac area's encode/decode round-trip test (< 10 mK) must pass before THM-19; THM-19 adds a timing guard (10k prims at 1 Hz < 100 ms). If either fails, switch to a per-material-class temperature texture/atlas indexed by material ID instead of per-prim attributes.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: The thermal solver needs per-facet sky-view factor and solar shadow state over the whole spin-up history; the renderer's AO AOV is per-pixel at render time only and cannot provide history.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: THM-19 design: bake a per-prim sky-view factor attribute once per scene and use an analytic/unshadowed flag during spin-up; measure the resulting t0 bias against a run with true shadow history on a small scene (expect < 1 K for open ground, larger under overhangs) and document in the granularity ADR.

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Skill line 36 lists NewtonCoolingSolver for 'a parked car cooling' and §6.6 says 'Newton cooling is exactly right' for a recently parked vehicle, but §6.5 says Newton is wrong for anything 'exchanging with a cold sky' — a parked car's skin at night does exactly that. Newton is right for the residual engine heat, not for the panels.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Assign regimes explicitly in THM-13/14: engine-bay residual heat → Newton; skin panels → energy balance. A THM-12 test compares a parked black panel at night under clear vs overcast sky and requires a > 1 K difference (Newton alone would give 0).

ambiguities_and_risks.description: Local environment: pytest is not installed for the python on PATH, so `make check` has not been verified as green at the scaffold baseline.
ambiguities_and_risks.how_to_verify: Run `make install && make check` before the first thermal commit; if the baseline fails, fix it in a separate chore commit.

non_negotiables_touched: #1 Engine-free core — every thermal module (weather, convection, solar, sky_longwave, energy_balance, solvers/*, spinup, field, vehicle/*, traces) is pure NumPy/SciPy under src/irsim/thermal; tests/unit/test_layering.py already parametrises over src/irsim/**/*.py and forbids omni/pxr/isaacsim/warp/carb, so every new file is enforced automatically. Only THM-19 (thermal tick driver) lives in src/irsim_isaac and is @pytest.mark.isaac.

#2 float32 or better where temperature flows — solvers integrate in float64; ThermalField.temperature_at returns float32 with a dtype assertion and raises on float16 (THM-11 test: float64-vs-float32 < 10 mK over 48 h; float16 raises). THM-09 and THM-17 reject float16 inputs and imported files. The encoded-T boundary c = (T−200)/800 stays float32 (isaac area's < 10 mK round-trip test, THM-19).

#3 Noise in radiance/electron space, never Kelvin — not exercised by this area, but enforced negatively: the thermal path is fully deterministic (THM-11 bit-identical rerun test); no random term exists anywhere in src/irsim/thermal.

#4 Kirchhoff closure — the thermal layer must not author a second emissivity: ThermalProperties.emissivity is populated from the material's optical data by the loader, and THM-18's MaterialThermalConfig uses extra='forbid' so an `emissivity` key inside `thermal:` is a ValidationError (test in THM-18). The library-wide closure test itself belongs to the materials area.

#6 One WeatherSeries feeds thermal and atmosphere — WeatherSeries is defined in irsim.thermal.weather (THM-01) as an array-only object with a content_hash; the loader is a separate function (THM-02); ThermalField and Atmosphere constructors take the object and have no file-path parameter; the Scene builder injects the same instance into both and asserts identity (THM-18 tests: introspection of constructor signatures, `thermal.weather is atmosphere.weather`, mismatched objects raise). The hash also keys the spin-up cache (THM-10) so a weather change can never reuse stale thermal history.

The equation contradicts its own prose and carries a stray exponent c.

docs/physics-model.md §6.4 line 410 claims the RK2 stability limit 'for thin painted metal (C1 ~ 5 kJ·m⁻²·K⁻¹) lands around 60–200 s' while prescribing a 1–60 s step. With the §16.2 car-paint row (line 1265: ρ 7800, c_p 470, k 45) and §12.3's thickness 1.2 mm (line 913), C1 = 4399 J·m⁻²·K⁻¹ and 1/R12 = 37,500 W·m⁻²·K⁻¹, so the bound is 0.24 s; 60–200 s (actually 837 s) only holds if the 1/R12 conduction term is omitted. The example, the step range and the two-node model cannot all be true for the material the example names.
